title: Understanding Datasets, Data Points, Features, and Labels
introduction: In machine learning, data is the foundation. Knowing how a dataset is organized helps you prepare the right information for a model to learn and make predictions.

sections.heading: What Is a Dataset?
sections.subheading: A collection of data used for learning
paragraphs: A dataset is a group of related data that we use to train or test a machine‑learning model. It contains many examples that share the same structure.
Think of it as a spreadsheet that holds all the information the model needs to see.

example.title: Fruit Price Dataset
example.content: A simple dataset might have columns for fruit name, weight, color, and price. Each row records one fruit sold at a market.

sections.heading: Data Points and Records
paragraphs: A data point, also called a record, is a single entry in the dataset. It holds the values for all columns for one example.
In the fruit dataset, one data point could be a single apple with its weight, color, and price.

example.title: One Record of a Fruit
example.content: Row 3: Apple, 150 g, Red, $1.20 – this whole row is one data point.

sections.heading: Rows and Columns
paragraphs: Rows run horizontally and list individual data points. Columns run vertically and define the type of information stored, such as weight or price.
The table shape lets us easily see patterns across many rows and compare values in each column.

sections.heading: Features (Input Variables)
sections.subheading: What the model looks at to make predictions
paragraphs: Features are the columns that provide information to the model. They are the inputs the model uses to learn relationships.
In our example, weight and color are features because they help the model guess the price.

example.title: Features in Fruit Example
example.content: Features: Weight (g) and Color. The model will read these values for each fruit.

sections.heading: Labels and Targets (Output Variables)
sections.subheading: What the model tries to predict
paragraphs: A label or target is the column the model aims to predict. It is the answer we want the model to learn.
In the fruit dataset, the price column is the label because we want the model to estimate the price from weight and color.

example.title: Label in Fruit Example
example.content: Label: Price ($). The model learns to output a price based on the given features.

practice.title: Identify Features and Labels
practice.instruction:
Look at the small table below and write down which columns are features and which column is the label:
| Fruit | Weight (g) | Color | Price ($) |
|-------|------------|-------|-----------|
| Apple | 150        | Red   | 1.20      |
| Banana| 120        | Yellow| 0.80      |
Explain your choice in one sentence for each.

keyTakeaways: A dataset is a structured collection of data points used for training models.
Features are input columns that help the model learn; labels are the output columns the model predicts.
Rows represent individual data points, while columns represent specific attributes like features or labels.

mcqs.question: What best describes a dataset in machine learning?
options: A single numeric value used for calculation
A collection of related data used to train or test a model
A computer program that runs algorithms
A hardware component that stores memory
mcqs.explanation: A dataset is defined as a structured group of data points that are used for training or testing a machine‑learning model.

mcqs.question: In the fruit price dataset, which of the following is a data point?
options: The entire table containing all fruits
mcqs.explanation: A data point (or record) is a single row that holds values for all columns, such as the apple example.

mcqs.question: Which statement correctly distinguishes rows and columns in a table?
options: Rows list attributes, while columns list individual observations
Rows run vertically and columns run horizontally
Rows run horizontally and represent data points; columns run vertically and define attributes
Rows and columns can be used interchangeably
mcqs.explanation: Rows are horizontal entries that correspond to individual data points, and columns are vertical headings that define each attribute like weight or price.

mcqs.question: Which columns are considered features in the fruit dataset?
mcqs.explanation: Features are the input variables; in this example weight and color provide information for the model to predict price.

mcqs.question: If a model is trained to predict the price of fruit, what is the label (target) column?
mcqs.explanation: The label or target is the column the model aims to predict, which is the price column in this dataset.
